deltas.owner_words: The start-up failure card has no logo and no "Reload the page" button. The design puts the on_light logo (on_dark in the dark theme) at the top of the card, with a Reload button under the message. The build put those two logos in a page footer instead, and the design has no logo in the footer. The asset checks R8.17 and R8.18 pass only because they compare the files' bytes, not where the logos are shown. Fix: move the <picture> into the #startup-error card and add the Reload button. Nothing was rendered: this rests on the served HTML, CSS and scripts read over HTTP. observed_on says "browser" only because the review schema has no value for a read that is not rendered.

Recommendation for the next design revision, not decided in this review: Out-of-range messages are the raw RangeError text with internal names and no units, for example "m1 must be a number from 0.1 to 10" (friction says "inclineDeg", trajectory "angleDeg" and "dragCoefficient"). An empty prediction gets the same generic message, and the summary is always headed "Check these values". The mockup shows "m₁ must be from 0.1 to 10 kg — you entered 12.", a counted heading ("Two things to fix before you run:") and "Enter your prediction to run the experiment." The design's notes also say "the RangeError message", so the next design revision should make binding the player-facing wording (symbol, unit, the value entered), and the build should then follow it. Nothing was rendered: this rests on the served HTML, CSS and scripts read over HTTP. observed_on says "browser" only because the review schema has no value for a read that is not rendered.

After a run the Run button still reads "Run the experiment". The mockups change it to "Run again". Nothing was rendered: this rests on the served HTML, CSS and scripts read over HTTP. observed_on says "browser" only because the review schema has no value for a read that is not rendered.

The 3D-unavailable notice uses different words from the design: "The 3D view is unavailable / Your browser could not load three.js…" where the design has "The 3D view couldn't load / The 3D library didn't arrive, so there's no animation this time. Nothing was rendered: this rests on the served HTML, CSS and scripts read over HTTP. observed_on says "browser" only because the review schema has no value for a read that is not rendered.

Nothing was rendered: this rests on the served HTML, CSS and scripts read over HTTP. observed_on says "browser" only because the review schema has no value for a read that is not rendered.

Recommendation for the next design revision, not decided in this review: The prediction slider runs from −30 to 30 m/s in the build; the mockup shows −10 to 10. The build is right and the design is wrong: an elastic collision can give v₂′ up to about 29.6 m/s (m₁ = 10 kg, m₂ = 0.1 kg, v₁ = 10, v₂ = −10), so −10 to 10 would refuse correct answers. The owner agrees the design is wrong and the build is right; the next design revision should change it to −30 to 30. Nothing was rendered: this rests on the served HTML, CSS and scripts read over HTTP. observed_on says "browser" only because the review schema has no value for a read that is not rendered.

deltas.owner_words: The Alpha's header shows the placeholder logo (PLACEHOLDER (on_dark), digest 6a8c47e8…), not the approved logo@2 on_dark (digest 1b0c17ab…). This is not a defect of this candidate: it was deployed at 13:24 UTC, before the logo was approved at 15:00, and the placeholder was correct then. Main already holds the approved on_dark logo in public/assets/logo.svg (commit 53efa50), byte-identical to the design's on_dark.svg. The difference goes away when an Alpha is deployed from main. Nothing to change in the design or the code; only a redeploy is needed. The approved logo's 3:1 viewBox fits the page's 108x36 slot unchanged.

The design's favicon slot (default variant, still the engine placeholder) is not on the page. index.html has no rel=icon link, and /favicon.svg answers 404. Change: serve design/assets/favicon/default.svg as public/favicon.svg and link it from index.html with rel=icon type=image/svg+xml. No specification criterion names the favicon, so this breaks none.

From reading app.mjs, not from use: the design says focus stays on a row's Watered button while it logs. When the button is pressed, the code rebuilds the whole list and disables the new button, so keyboard focus drops to the page body until the request ends. It then comes back to the button. Change: keep the row's button element in place while it logs (mark it aria-disabled and ignore presses rather than disabling and replacing it), so focus never leaves it.

From reading app.mjs, not from use: the design announces 'Logged a watering for <name>.' in a polite live region above the list. The code creates a new live-region element, already holding the text, on every render. Screen readers often do not announce a live region that arrives with its text already in it, so the confirmation may go unheard. The text itself is right. Change: keep one status element in the page and change only its text.
